request: what does 347 mean in place value?

beats.intent: Three 10 by 10 squares of hundreds, four columns of tens and seven single ones
beats.narration: Three hundred and forty seven is three hundreds, four tens and seven ones.
beats.code:
hundred = lambda c=BLUE: VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.12, color=c, fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0.5) for _ in range(100)]).arrange_in_grid(10, 10, buff=0.01)
ten = lambda c=GREEN: VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.12, color=c, fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0.5) for _ in range(10)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.01)
one = lambda c=YELLOW: Square(side_length=0.12, color=c, fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_width=0.5)

stage.title("Place value: 347")
blocks = VGroup(VGroup(*[hundred() for _ in range(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
                VGroup(*[ten() for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1),
                VGroup(*[one() for _ in range(7)]).arrange_in_grid(4, 2, buff=0.05)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6, aligned_edge=DOWN)
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b) for b in blocks], lag_ratio=0.4))
stage.add(blocks)

beats.intent: Each group labelled 300, 40 and 7
beats.narration: The hundreds are worth three hundred, the tens forty, the ones seven.
beats.code:
for g, t in zip(blocks, ("300", "40", "7")):
    stage.label(g, t, direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The blocks beside 347 = 300 + 40 + 7
beats.narration: The digits tell you how many of each.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"347 = 300 + 40 + 7")

request: why do you carry a 1 when adding 58 + 27?

beats.intent: Blocks for 58 (5 tens, 8 ones) and 27 (2 tens, 7 ones)
beats.narration: Fifty eight is five tens and eight ones; twenty seven is two tens and seven ones.
beats.code:
hundred = lambda c=BLUE: VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.12, color=c, fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0.5) for _ in range(100)]).arrange_in_grid(10, 10, buff=0.01)
ten = lambda c=GREEN: VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.12, color=c, fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0.5) for _ in range(10)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.01)
one = lambda c=YELLOW: Square(side_length=0.12, color=c, fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_width=0.5)

stage.title("Carrying in 58 + 27")
tens = VGroup(*[ten() for _ in range(7)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1).shift(LEFT * 2)
ones = VGroup(*[one() for _ in range(15)]).arrange_in_grid(3, 5, buff=0.05).shift(RIGHT * 2)
stage.play(FadeIn(tens), FadeIn(ones))
stage.add(tens, ones)
stage.caption("7 tens and 15 ones")

beats.intent: Ten of the ones moved together into a new ten column
beats.narration: Fifteen ones is too many for one digit. Ten of them join into a new ten.
beats.code:
new_ten = ten(YELLOW).next_to(tens, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
stage.play(ReplacementTransform(VGroup(*ones[:10]), new_ten), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(new_ten)
stage.caption("8 tens and 5 ones")

beats.intent: 8 tens and 5 ones beside 58 + 27 = 85
beats.narration: Now there are eight tens and five ones: eighty five. The carried one is that new ten.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"58 + 27 = 85")

beats.intent: 84 dots in a grid
beats.narration: Eighty four sweets to share between four friends.
beats.code:
stage.title("84 ÷ 4 as sharing")
dots = draw_dots(stage, n=84, cols=12)

beats.intent: The dots coloured into four equal groups of 21
beats.narration: Deal them out one by one: each friend gets twenty one.
beats.code:
cols = [RED, GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW]
stage.play(*[dots[k].animate.set_color(cols[k % 4]) for k in range(84)], run_time=1.5)

beats.intent: Four boxes with 21 dots each beside 84 ÷ 4 = 21
beats.narration: Four groups of twenty one: eighty four divided by four is twenty one.
beats.code:
groups = VGroup(*[VGroup(*[dots[k] for k in range(g, 84, 4)]) for g in range(4)])
stage.play(*[grp.animate.arrange_in_grid(3, 7, buff=0.12).move_to(np.array([-4.5 + 3 * i, -0.3, 0])) for i, grp in enumerate(groups)], run_time=1.5)
stage.equation(r"84 \div 4 = 21")

request: what is the lowest common multiple of 4 and 6?

beats.intent: A number line from 0 to 24 with the multiples of 4 marked
beats.narration: Mark the multiples of four: four, eight, twelve, sixteen, twenty, twenty four.
beats.code:
stage.title("The LCM of 4 and 6")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(0, 24))
for m in range(4, 25, 4):
    mark_point(stage, nl, m, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: The multiples of 6 marked below in green
beats.narration: Now the multiples of six: six, twelve, eighteen, twenty four.
beats.code:
for m in range(6, 25, 6):
    mark_point(stage, nl, m, color=GREEN, label=str(m), direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: 12 ringed as the first number marked twice
beats.narration: The first number on both lists is twelve: the lowest common multiple.
beats.code:
ring = Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW).move_to(nl.n2p(12))
stage.play(Create(ring))
stage.add(ring)
stage.equation(r"\mathrm{lcm}(4, 6) = 12")

beats.intent: A 1 by 12 row of squares
beats.narration: Twelve squares in one row: one times twelve.
beats.code:
stage.title("Factors of 12")
row = lambda r, c, col: VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.35, color=col, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(r * c)]).arrange_in_grid(r, c, buff=0.03)
a = row(1, 12, BLUE).shift(UP * 2)
stage.play(FadeIn(a))
stage.add(a)
stage.label(a, "1 × 12", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: A 2 by 6 and a 3 by 4 rectangle of the same 12 squares
beats.narration: Rearrange them: two rows of six, three rows of four.
beats.code:
b = row(2, 6, GREEN).shift(LEFT * 2.5 + DOWN * 0.3)
c = row(3, 4, YELLOW).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + DOWN * 0.3)
stage.play(FadeIn(b), FadeIn(c))
stage.add(b, c)
stage.label(b, "2 × 6", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(c, "3 × 4", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The rectangles beside the factors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12
beats.narration: Every rectangle's sides are factors: one, two, three, four, six and twelve.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"12:\ 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12")

request: what does the square root of 10 mean?

beats.intent: A 3 by 3 square of area 9 labelled side 3
beats.narration: A square of area nine has side three: the square root of nine is three.
beats.code:
stage.title("Square roots as sides")
nine = Square(side_length=3 * 0.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.4).shift(LEFT * 2.5)
stage.play(Create(nine))
stage.add(nine)
stage.label(nine, "area 9, side 3", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: A slightly bigger square of area 10 beside it
beats.narration: A square of area ten must be a little bigger.
beats.code:
ten_sq = Square(side_length=np.sqrt(10) * 0.8, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.4).shift(RIGHT * 2.2)
stage.play(Create(ten_sq))
stage.add(ten_sq)
stage.label(ten_sq, "area 10", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The bigger square beside √10 ≈ 3.16
beats.narration: Its side is the square root of ten, about three point one six, just over three.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\sqrt{10} \approx 3.16")

request: why is 0.5 × 0.4 smaller than both numbers?

beats.intent: A unit square with its left 0.5 shaded blue
beats.narration: Take a one by one square and shade half its width.
beats.code:
stage.title("0.5 × 0.4 as an area")
sq = Square(side_length=4, color=WHITE)
half = Rectangle(width=2, height=4, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.35).align_to(sq, LEFT)
stage.play(Create(sq), FadeIn(half))
stage.add(sq, half)

beats.intent: The bottom 0.4 of the square shaded green, overlapping the blue
beats.narration: Now shade the bottom four tenths of its height.
beats.code:
low = Rectangle(width=4, height=1.6, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.35).align_to(sq, DOWN)
stage.play(FadeIn(low))
stage.add(low)

beats.intent: The overlap 0.5 by 0.4 lit in yellow beside 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2
beats.narration: The overlap is point five by point four: a fifth of the square. Multiplying by numbers less than one makes things smaller.
beats.code:
both = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.6, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8).align_to(sq, DOWN + LEFT)
stage.play(FadeIn(both))
stage.add(both)
stage.equation(r"0.5 \times 0.4 = 0.2")
